build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Travelers present documents that the player can drag, inspect, and compare against a rulebook on the desk workspace. Score 0 if no document inspection exists.
The player stamps documents APPROVE or DENY, and incorrect decisions result in citations that reduce end-of-day pay. Score 0 if there is no approval/denial mechanic or no consequence for errors.
Each day has a time limit and pay is per-person processed, creating speed-vs-accuracy tension. Score 0 if there is no time pressure or pay-per-person system.
End-of-day shows earnings vs family expenses (rent, heat, food, medicine), and the player must allocate limited funds to keep the family alive. Score 0 if no family/expense system exists.
Moral choice events present dilemmas (bribes, helping refugees, reporting corruption) that affect story progression and have visible consequences. Score 0 if no moral choices exist.
Rules change each day with at least 10 days of escalating complexity: new document types, new checks (photo match, expiration, permits, vaccinations). Score 0 if rules never change.
At least 4 distinct document types (passport, work permit, vaccination card, entry ticket) with different fields to verify. Score 0 if only one document type exists.
Travelers have varied appearances, nationalities, and stories, with at least 3 story-event characters who recur across days. Score 0 if all travelers are identical.
Multiple ending conditions based on accumulated choices: compliance ending, resistance ending, escape ending, and family-loss ending. Score 0 if only one ending exists.
An end-of-day report shows people processed, citations received, earnings, expenses paid, and family status with narrative text. Score 0 if days end abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name and bleak checkpoint-themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to day-start briefing to inspection gameplay to end-of-day report to story events without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The workspace clearly shows the desk with document inspection area, rulebook reference, stamps, and queue indicator in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine what to check or how to act.
Player actions produce visible feedback: stamping shows ink effect, discrepancies can be highlighted, citations flash warnings, and travelers react to decisions. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, desk workspace, documents, travelers, reports, and story screens with a consistent bleak bureaucratic palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Documents, traveler portraits, desk elements, stamps, and rulebook pages use real illustrated art with distinct designs. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation adds life: documents slide onto desk, stamps press with weight, travelers approach and leave, pages turn, and citations appear with emphasis. Score 0 if all elements are static.
UI panels use styled themed widgets with bureaucratic framing, typewriter fonts, or period-appropriate styling rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
